A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ALINE, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-E. Shared material can be reliably matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ALINE experiments on regression, Bayesian experimental design, and simulated psychometric inference, including performance curves, timing measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds HPO-B evaluations, vsOED comparisons, and psychometric acquisition trajectories testing runtime flexibility.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, inference and acquisition heads, target-conditioned attention, rewards, warm-up procedure, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Revised factorization expressions and the explanation of gradient handling clarify the existing method rather than establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds real-world HPO-B performance-landscape tasks: rpart (6D), svm (8D), ranger (9D), and xgboost (16D), substantially extending the earlier simulated and analytic benchmarks. It also explicitly tests target switching during acquisition and target combinations unseen during training.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds vsOED as an evaluated comparator for both Location Finding and CES; the existing external comparator sets remain. The separate ALINE(full) versus ALINE(targeted) comparison from v1 Appendix D.3 is removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include HPO-B predefined training/test partitions and RMSE after 30 queries, switching psychometric targets at step 16, and testing all four parameters after training on two separate target pairs. The added vsOED experiment specifies its training configuration. Settings for the retained benchmark experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Figure A9 quantitatively compares targeted and full-parameter acquisition. v2 removes this analysis and adds two qualitative demonstrations in Figure A8: adaptation after a target switch and generalization to an unseen target combination. Other supplementary acquisition, posterior, and distribution-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing repeated-run counts and mean/95% confidence interval or mean/standard deviation reporting practices are retained. HPO-B results reuse confidence-interval reporting; additional result rows and revised interval values do not establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds HPO-B results, vsOED scores and timings, and flexibility trajectories, while removing the targeted/full RMSE curves. Under unchanged stated CES settings, ALINE's Table 2 EIG lower bound changes from 14.37 ± 0.08 to 13.50 ± 0.15; RL-BOED remains 14.60 ± 0.10. New HPO-B ALINE RMSEs are 0.01, 0.03, 0.02, and 0.03 for rpart, svm, ranger, and xgboost, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly assumes a well-specified generative model and clarifies the factorization approximations in Equations 5-6. Appendix A.3 corrects the erroneous sum-of-densities identity to a sum of log densities and fixes joint-distribution conditioning in the variational-bound derivation. The propositions and overall proof strategy remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: joint amortized inference and acquisition, self-estimated information-gain rewards, and flexible inference targets. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning autoregressive reward computation costs, applicability to implicit likelihoods, shared-backbone efficiency, and transfer across HPO tasks. The CES discussion changes from performance comparable to RL-BOED to explicitly acknowledging its advantage. Existing limitations concerning priors, marginal inference, distribution shift, and design spaces remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2.2 adds vsOED architecture, optimizer, replay-buffer, and exploration-noise details; Appendix E adds its code source and license. Section 3.3 newly specifies that policy-loss gradients do not propagate into the inference network. Existing ALINE hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and project code link remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds vsOED to the discussion of prior methods combining amortized inference and design, alongside RL-sCEE. It also adds references on HPO-B, environmental sensor placement, and efficient autoregressive inference. The broader positioning relative to ACE, neural processes, and amortized experimental design is retained.

P1.justification: Related work moves from a standalone section into Background, with subsequent sections renumbered. Local explanations, author affiliations, acknowledgements, and the conference header are updated. Most existing prose and the overall exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The architecture schematic moves from v1 Figure A1 to v2 Figure 2. v2 adds HPO-B Table A3 and a vsOED row in Table 2, replaces the targeted/full RMSE figure with two acquisition-trajectory panels, and relocates other displays. Matched existing figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: The HPO-B evaluation broadens empirical support beyond the earlier simulated benchmarks, and vsOED supplies a relevant additional comparison. Proof corrections and clearer gradient documentation improve precision. These gains are tempered by removal of the quantitative targeted/full ablation: its replacements are qualitative, and HPO-B advantages over ACE-US are small or tied, with overlapping reported intervals.
